title: A one-step transition gives a bounded run
statement: Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, with initial label $\ell$, register assignment $\rho$, and input position $p$, and target label-or-halted-state $q$, register assignment $\rho'$, input position $p'$, and output string $e$. Suppose that for every output string $o$, one step from the state with label $\ell$, registers $\rho$, input position $p$, and output $o$ yields the state with label-or-halted-state $q$, registers $\rho'$, input position $p'$, and output $o$ followed by $e$. Then from that initial state the program reaches the specified target state within at most one step, appending $e$ to every initial output string.

Let $P$ be a counter program on a binary input $x$, let $\ell$ be a label,
$\ell'$ a label or the halted state, $\rho, \rho'$ register vectors, $p, p'$
input positions and $e$ a bit string.  If for every output $o$ one step of $P$
on $x$ maps the state with label $\ell$, registers $\rho$, $p$ symbols read and
output $o$ to the state with label $\ell'$, registers $\rho'$, $p'$ symbols read
and output $o\,e$, then from $(\ell, \rho, p)$ the program reaches
$(\ell', \rho', p')$ within one step while appending $e$ to its output.
